From pixels to a small CNN on BloodMNIST: what earns a keep

From pixel logistic regression to a small CNN: what earns a keep under a measured floor on 8-class blood-cell microscopy images (BloodMNIST, official split), and how far does a CPU-budget CNN get toward the published MedMNIST baselines?

study: 21-bloodmnist-cnn · metric: val_macro_f1 (primary) · domain: medical image classification (hematology microscopy) · 2026-11-03

1. The Question 2. The Method 3. The Data 4. The Journey 5. Findings 6. Coding Advice 7. Next Steps

The question

A practitioner trains a small CNN on a benchmark of blood-cell photographs, changes one thing at a time, and watches a number go up. The decision this study informs is: when is a change a real improvement and not seed luck or the wobble of a small evaluation set? The concrete task is BloodMNIST, eight classes of normal blood cells at 28 × 28 pixels, official split, on a CPU budget. The registered questions ask how far a linear softmax on raw pixels gets (RQ1), whether the recipe two-block CNN clears it by more than the measured floor (RQ2), which single change earns a keep once a CNN is in place (RQ3), and whether the final incumbent holds on the sealed official test split and how it sits against MedMNIST v2's ResNet-18 (28) accuracy of 0.958 (RQ4).

Takeaways

  • The recipe CNN barely beat a linear model. The anchor scored a macro-F1 of 0.7189 against 0.6903 for pixel-linear softmax, a gap of 0.65 keep bars. Prediction P2 (at least 0.85) was refuted.
  • Two changes earned a keep. Batch normalization, once a running-statistics bug was repaired (E0004, 0.8960), and a four-lever bundle (E0008, 0.9461) whose gain cannot be attributed to any single lever.
  • The sealed run held. One access to the official test split scored a macro-F1 of 0.9465 and an accuracy of 0.9527, 0.0053 below the published 0.958, which is indistinguishable from ResNet-18 (28) at this test size.

Scope travels with every number on this page: all scores are image-level. The official MedMNIST split is not grouped by patient or smear, so nothing here estimates performance on a new patient. The final records (claim totals, the referee verdict, the finalization label) are copied from the study's state files into the evidence block in section 5.

The method taught

Intuition: stencils, then sliding stencilsThe load-bearing mathTwo noises, one keep barThe from-scratch pieces

Intuition: stencils, then sliding stencils

BloodMNIST is photographs of single cells, centre-cropped and shrunk to 28 × 28 RGB. The classes differ by colour, size and nucleus shape. A linear softmax on pixels gives each class one template image; a cell is called whatever template it overlaps best. A convolution is a small learned stencil applied at every position (weight sharing), so features need not be relearned per location, and stacking layers lets later filters combine earlier ones. Counted from model.py, the linear model has 18,824 parameters and the anchor CNN 19,912, so the first comparison spends the same budget two ways.

The load-bearing math

Training minimizes softmax cross-entropy, with augmentation stated as a prior: each training image is replaced by a random member of its dihedral orbit (four rotations, each with or without a flip; exact pixel permutations at 28 pixels).

Batch normalization standardizes each channel per mini-batch, then learns a scale and shift back. At evaluation the batch statistics are replaced by population statistics. The way those are obtained turns out to be the study's most expensive lesson (section 6).

The primary metric is macro-F1, an unweighted mean of per-class F1 scores, each read off the confusion table. Accuracy is a prevalence-weighted mean of recalls. Macro-F1 is a ratio of sums per class, not a mean over items, so a bootstrap of it must recompute it on every re-draw.

Two noises, one keep bar

Fit noise is how much a score moves when the seeds are redrawn: the instability of the fitting procedure. Item noise is how much it moves had the development images been another draw from the same smears: the precision of the ruler. A seed array shrinks the first, not the second, because every seed is scored on the same images. The keep bar is therefore set from an item bootstrap of the anchor's pinned confusion tables:

Here is the macro-F1 on bootstrap re-draw of the development items. The measured bar is 0.0438, and the half-range term, not twice the standard deviation, is the one that binds.

The from-scratch pieces

The study is run through a notary: every candidate is a three-seed array (seeds 0, 1, 2), and the decision is made on the seed mean against the bar. The weight-sharing idea is one line: the same filter is applied at every position,

and a third conv-pool block raises the receptive field from 8 to 18 pixels, about the whole cell, which is why depth was a candidate lever and not just more capacity.

The data story

ShapeGotchas the audit caughtThe call

Shape

The source is MedMNIST v2's bloodmnist.npz: uint8 images of shape 28 × 28 × 3, eight classes of expert-labelled normal blood cells, with the official 7:1:2 partitions kept (data.split.kind: predefined). Train has 11,959 images, development 1,709 and the sealed test split 3,413, after removal of near-duplicates (below). Class imbalance is moderate, about 2.7 to 1 between the largest and smallest class, so macro-F1 is the primary and accuracy is printed beside it. Two development classes (basophil and lymphocyte) have only 122 items, so per-class recall there is coarse.

Gotchas the audit caught

  • Near-duplicates across partitions (a blocker, repaired). The dHash audit at 4 bits found 3 of 1,712 development and 7 of 3,421 test images with a copy in train (nine byte-identical groups span splits, and one cross-split pair carries conflicting labels). The decision was to remove them, not tolerate them: prepare.py drops 3 development and 8 test items, and the re-run audit passes 8 of 8. Published MedMNIST numbers are on 1,712 / 3,421 images, a difference every comparison here states.
  • The split is image-level. MedMNIST describes a random 7:1:2 split with no patient or slide identifier, so group overlap is unknown and cannot be audited. Scores answer “new cells from the same smears and lab”, never “a new patient”.
  • Unnormalized uint8 pixels. Channel standard deviations differ (blue is far narrower than green); normalization is a training choice, not a data property.

The call

The data card's decision is GO with cautions: the one blocker was removed before the gate, and the two cautions (image-level scope, imbalance with coarse per-class estimates) travel with every claim. The data card's clean-room leakage row 4 asked for a label-shuffled harness control to be reproduced from train.py; that control was never run and is a disclosed gap (see sections 5 and 7). The harness is checked only by the analytic chance levels and the notary's rejection of near-constant predictions.

Development frontier

Phase 0 measured the floor on the anchor (E0001) and set the bar. The pixel-linear baseline (E0002) came in 0.65 bars below the anchor, so the recipe CNN barely beat a stencil model. Plain batch normalization (E0003) collapsed to a macro-F1 of 0.3005: a bug in inference, not a verdict on the idea. Recomputing the running statistics on the training set (E0004) scored 0.8960, a gain of 4.04 bars over the anchor and the first keep.

What each candidate did, against its bar

After E0004, flip/rotation augmentation alone (E0005) moved the score by -0.0067, unresolved at this budget. A third conv block (E0006, +0.0326) and 4,000 steps (E0007, +0.0280) were positive on every seed pair but short of the bar by 0.0112 and 0.0158; the bar was not relaxed after the fact. The registered bundle of all four levers (E0008) scored 0.9461, +0.0501 over E0004 and 0.0062 above the bar, but its margins over the depth-only and schedule-only runs (+0.0175 and +0.0221) are inside the bar. The bundle's gain cannot be attributed to any one lever.

Seed spread: why the bar is not the whole story

The anchor's seed-block spread (sd 0.0472) is 3.94 times the item-bootstrap sd of 0.0120 that sets the bar, which falsified a prior from the method card. Once batch normalization was in, per-candidate seed sds fell to about 0.007 to 0.015, so the anchor's fit noise does not describe the incumbent.

Sealed confirmation (separate evidence)

After a mandatory dry run, the incumbent configuration was run once on the sealed official test split (E0009). The run refits the same recipe on train plus development, so it scores E0008's recipe, not E0008's weights. It scored a macro-F1 of 0.9465, +0.0004 against development, and the incumbent replicated with difference 0 (klein replicate). The final headroom of 1.23 means a further keep would need a macro-F1 of 0.9899, so the frontier is nearly closed under the anchor's bar. The bar was measured at the anchor, not at the incumbent (see section 7).

Verdicts

  • RQ1 (C1). Pixel-linear softmax reached 0.6903 macro-F1 (accuracy 0.7353), far above the chance controls (prior-matched random 0.125, majority class 0.0408) and inside the prior range of 0.50 to 0.85. P1 supported.
  • RQ2 (C2). The recipe CNN cleared pixel-linear by only 0.0286, inside the bar, and far below the prior of 0.85. P2 refuted.
  • RQ3 (C3, C4). Working batch normalization is the only single change to earn a keep; depth and schedule are positive but sub-bar, augmentation alone is unresolved, and the bundle is supported but not attributable. P3 supported (the verdict is about the bundle).
  • RQ4 (C5). On the sealed test split the incumbent configuration scored a macro-F1 of 0.9465 and an accuracy of 0.9527. P4 supported. P5 is supported arithmetically (below 0.958), but the gap of 0.0053 is about 1.5 binomial standard errors, so the honest reading is indistinguishable from ResNet-18 (28). This is the only level the study confirms: development-to-development comparisons stay exploratory.

Per-class effects are uneven

From E0001 to E0008 basophil recall rose from 0.2562 to 0.9201 and immature-granulocyte recall from 0.7046 to 0.9149. Monocyte recall fell from 0.8345 at E0004 to 0.7949 at E0008, and monocytes remain the weakest class on the sealed test (0.8582). That drop is not an established effect: on 143 development monocytes it is about 1.2 to 1.3 binomial standard errors of one recall (not a test statistic for the difference), and the per-seed recalls of the two runs overlap widely. Its cause is unresolved.

Calibration came along: expected calibration error fell from 0.0828 at the anchor to 0.0125 at E0008 (0.0086 on the sealed test), and log-loss from 0.6660 to 0.1333, so no recalibration step was needed.

Surprises, with their status

  • Seed luck exceeded item noise. Measured: fit noise was 3.94 times item noise at the anchor. The mechanism proposed in the findings (unstable, under-trained optimisation, claim C11) is untested: the learning-rate schedule was never varied.
  • Batch normalization first measured as a catastrophe. Measured: recomputing the statistics (E0004) scored 0.5955 higher than E0003. The explanation that the default running averages lag weights that are still moving (claim C7) rests on an off-loop seed-0 diagnostic that is not evidence, so it stays an untested interpretation.
  • Different failure patterns for the linear model and the anchor. Measured per-class recall differs; reading it as “colour stencils versus local texture” is an untested interpretation, since no run probed what either model uses.
  • No development-to-test drop after selection (+0.0004). Selection optimism and the larger refit push in opposite directions and one sealed number cannot separate them; this is unresolved, not “no optimism”.

Scope and the control that does not exist

Everything above is image-level on the official split, not patient-grouped, and the sealed comparison with MedMNIST is on 3,413 rather than 3,421 test images, a three-seed mean, and a train-plus-development refit. The label-shuffled harness control was never run; this is a disclosed gap, the harness resting on analytic chance levels alone. The study counts seven frontier comparisons with no family-wise correction, which is why every development comparison is exploratory. Four of five method-card priors about noise and class difficulty were falsified.

Vision-model coding advice

The network: model.py at E0008The recipe: train.py at E0008The sealed cell: train.py at E0009Pitfalls and war stories that bit this study

This section walks the source that was actually executed. model.py and train.py are the mutable surface, which the notary restores after every non-keep, so the files on disk are not a reliable witness. Each listing below is read from the candidate commit a named run executed: the incumbent E0008 (development) and the sealed E0009 (test). E0009's candidate diff was empty, so its train.py is byte-identical to E0008's; the two provenance lines show the same hash. No verifier script is declared: the metric comes from the library evaluator kleinlib.eval_multiclass.evaluate_multiclass, which refuses non-finite probabilities and collapsed single-class predictions, prints the metric block and pins the confusion table.

The network: model.py at E0008

Three conv-BN-ReLU blocks (32, 64, 128 channels), max-pool after the first two, global average pooling and a linear head. The third block lifts the receptive field to about the whole cell, and global pooling makes the head independent of the image size.

model.py · executed by E0008 (development, track primary) at commit 80be6152e0b1 · sha256 1321e4543b8a… 
"""The network (part of the mutable surface, recipe cv-classify)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import torch
from torch import nn


class SmallCNN(nn.Module):
    """Two conv blocks + a linear head — the honest small baseline for small images."""

    def __init__(self, in_channels: int, n_classes: int, width: int = 32) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(in_channels, width, 3, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(width),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.MaxPool2d(2),
            nn.Conv2d(width, 2 * width, 3, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(2 * width),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.MaxPool2d(2),
            nn.Conv2d(2 * width, 4 * width, 3, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(4 * width),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1),
            nn.Flatten(),
            nn.Linear(4 * width, n_classes),
        )

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.body(x)

The recipe: train.py at E0008

Four things deserve a close read. (1) d4 applies the dihedral symmetries to the training batch, inside the loop, from its own generator (SEED + 10_000), so the batch order stays identical to the anchor's at the same seed and an augmentation run is a paired comparison. (2) The budget is optimizer steps, not epochs, so runs compare across devices. (3) Batches come from iterate_minibatches, a streamed index shuffle, never a DataLoader over a TensorDataset. (4) After training, the BatchNorm running statistics are reset, set to a cumulative average (momentum = None) and recomputed over one pass of the training set in train mode with no gradient, before eval(). That block is the whole difference between E0003 and E0004.

train.py · executed by E0008 (development, track primary) at commit 80be6152e0b1 · sha256 134b0b84fcbe… 
"""The per-candidate training recipe (mutable surface with model.py; recipe cv-classify).

One run of this file is ONE seed of the candidate: `klein run-one` runs every seed
in `entrypoint.seeds` (setting KLEIN_SEED) and decides on the aggregate. Training
chatter may be printed freely before the final block (`entrypoint.printed: block`).
The budget is in optimizer STEPS, so CPU and GPU runs are comparable.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import time

import numpy as np
import torch

from kleinlib.data import load_items
from kleinlib.dl import report_usage, seed_everything
from kleinlib.eval_multiclass import evaluate_multiclass
from kleinlib.torch_device import pick_device
from kleinlib.torch_loop import iterate_minibatches
from model import SmallCNN

SMOKE = os.environ.get("KLEIN_SMOKE") == "1"
EXPERIMENT_ID = os.environ.get("KLEIN_EXPERIMENT_ID") or ("SMOKE" if SMOKE else None)
SEED = int(os.environ.get("KLEIN_SEED", "0"))

RECIPE = {"steps": 200 if SMOKE else 4000, "batch_size": 64, "lr": 3e-3, "weight_decay": 1e-4, "width": 32}


def load(ids: list[str]) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    import pandas as pd

    index = pd.read_csv("data/prepared/index.csv", dtype={"id": str})
    images = np.load("data/prepared/images.npy", mmap_mode="r")
    rows = index.reset_index().set_index("id").loc[ids, "index"].to_numpy()
    x = np.asarray(images[rows], dtype=np.float32)
    if images.dtype == np.uint8:
        x /= 255.0  # prepare.py keeps the source's uint8 pixels
    if x.ndim == 3:
        x = x[:, None, :, :]  # (N, 1, H, W)
    elif x.shape[-1] in (1, 3, 4):
        x = np.moveaxis(x, -1, 1)
    return x, index.set_index("id").loc[ids, "label"].to_numpy()


def d4(xb: torch.Tensor, aug_rng: np.random.Generator) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Random element of the dihedral group D4 per image (exact pixel permutations)."""
    k = aug_rng.integers(0, 4, len(xb))
    flip = aug_rng.random(len(xb)) < 0.5
    out = xb.clone()
    for r in (1, 2, 3):
        m = torch.from_numpy(k == r)
        if m.any():
            out[m] = torch.rot90(out[m], r, dims=(2, 3))
    m = torch.from_numpy(flip)
    if m.any():
        out[m] = out[m].flip(3)
    return out


def main() -> None:
    if EXPERIMENT_ID is None:
        raise SystemExit("run through `klein run-one` (or KLEIN_SMOKE=1 for a shape check)")
    t0 = time.time()
    seed_everything(SEED)
    fit_ids, eval_ids = load_items()
    x_fit, y_fit = load(fit_ids)
    x_eval, y_eval = load(eval_ids)
    classes = np.unique(np.concatenate([y_fit, y_eval]))
    device = pick_device()
    model = SmallCNN(x_fit.shape[1], len(classes), RECIPE["width"]).to(device)
    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=RECIPE["lr"], weight_decay=RECIPE["weight_decay"])
    loss_fn = torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    xt, yt = torch.from_numpy(x_fit), torch.from_numpy(y_fit.astype(np.int64))
    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
    aug_rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED + 10_000)  # its own generator: batch order matches the anchor
    step, fit_start = 0, time.time()
    while step < RECIPE["steps"]:
        for batch in iterate_minibatches(len(xt), RECIPE["batch_size"], shuffle=True, generator=rng):
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            loss = loss_fn(model(d4(xt[batch], aug_rng).to(device)), yt[batch].to(device))
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            step += 1
            if step % 250 == 0:
                print(f"step: {step} loss: {loss.item():.4f}")  # chatter: outside the final block
            if step >= RECIPE["steps"]:
                break
    # BatchNorm: recompute the running statistics as a cumulative average over one pass of the
    # TRAINING set (no grad), so inference does not depend on a lagging momentum average.
    bns = [mod for mod in model.modules() if isinstance(mod, torch.nn.BatchNorm2d)]
    for mod in bns:
        mod.reset_running_stats()
        mod.momentum = None
    model.train()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for batch in iterate_minibatches(len(xt), 256, shuffle=False, generator=None):
            model(xt[batch].to(device))
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        proba = torch.softmax(model(torch.from_numpy(x_eval).to(device)), dim=1).cpu().numpy().astype(np.float64)
    proba /= proba.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    report_usage(steps=step)
    evaluate_multiclass(
        y_eval,
        proba,
        labels=classes.tolist(),
        exp_id=EXPERIMENT_ID,
        metric_name="val_macro_f1",
        t0=t0,
        fit_seconds=time.time() - fit_start,
        train_n=len(fit_ids),
        extra={"steps": step, "seed": SEED},
        study_dir=".",
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

The sealed cell: train.py at E0009

The same bytes, run once on the official test split after a dry run. The sealed refit trains on train plus development (13,668 rows against 11,959), a difference that comes from the contract's partition and not from the code.

    # TRAINING set (no grad), so inference does not depend on a lagging momentum average.
    bns = [mod for mod in model.modules() if isinstance(mod, torch.nn.BatchNorm2d)]
    for mod in bns:
        mod.reset_running_stats()
        mod.momentum = None
    model.train()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for batch in iterate_minibatches(len(xt), 256, shuffle=False, generator=None):
            model(xt[batch].to(device))
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        proba = torch.softmax(model(torch.from_numpy(x_eval).to(device)), dim=1).cpu().numpy().astype(np.float64)
    proba /= proba.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    report_usage(steps=step)
    evaluate_multiclass(
        y_eval,
        proba,
        labels=classes.tolist(),
        exp_id=EXPERIMENT_ID,
        metric_name="val_macro_f1",
        t0=t0,
        fit_seconds=time.time() - fit_start,
        train_n=len(fit_ids),
        extra={"steps": step, "seed": SEED},
        study_dir=".",
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Pitfalls and war stories that bit this study

  1. Default BatchNorm inference cost a candidate. E0003 added BatchNorm2d and scored 0.3005 because evaluation used momentum-0.1 running averages. An off-loop diagnostic (one seed, not evidence) showed batch-statistics accuracy staying high while eval-mode accuracy collapsed, which points at the inference path. Before calling a normalization candidate a failure, compare train-mode and eval-mode outputs, and recompute the statistics on the training set. The mechanism (averages lagging weights that are still moving at a constant learning rate) is an untested interpretation.
  2. One bundle, one unattributed gain. E0008 changed four levers together. Budget the single-lever cells inside the phase cap, or the gain stays unattributed.
  3. Measure fit noise, not only item noise. The bar came from an item bootstrap; the seed-block spread was several times larger at the anchor. Read each keep together with its seed spread.
  4. A near-duplicate audit before training. Eleven cross-split near-duplicates were removed from the evaluation partitions; state that the official split is image-level, not patient-grouped.
  5. Compare a sealed number with a published one in standard errors. A gap under two binomial standard errors is “indistinguishable” whatever the arithmetic verdict of a rule says.
  6. Per-seed tables, not one aux row. The aux rows of the earliest runs hold only the last seed; read runs/E####/seeds.tsv for seed means.
  7. Run the label-shuffled control. This study did not; the harness check therefore rests on analytic chance levels alone.

What to try next

  1. Decompose E0008. Three registered cells of three seeds each: E0008 minus augmentation, minus the extra steps, minus the third block. This is the only way to attribute the bundle's gain and to resolve augmentation, which E0005 left open.
  2. Re-measure the keep bar at the incumbent. The item bootstrap ran on the anchor's confusion tables; rerun it on E0008's pinned tables before attempting another keep. At a headroom of 1.23 the frontier is nearly closed under the anchor's bar, and a bar measured near 0.95 is expected to be narrower.
  3. Run the missing harness control (label-shuffled training through train.py), and a learning-rate decay at matched steps, the one recipe difference to the MedMNIST ResNet that the study never varied.
  4. Measure transfer, not only fit: a patient-grouped or other-site blood-smear set, to answer the question that this image-level split cannot.
